qolFindings.title: The fingerprint cannot see a committed edit that keeps its stamp, and 03 names only in-flight edits of existing rows as the limit
qolFindings.evidence: src/persistence/stamp.ts TOUCH is max(?, updatedAt, createdAt), so a phone whose clock is behind leaves the stamp unchanged. The server accepts it: 20261026000000_upload_rules.sql refuses only a stamp lower than the stored one. The fingerprint covers table, id and stamp, so the same text comes out. Case E on Postgres, with the content changed on the server and the same stamp: 'kept', course erased. Reaching it needs a device holding only the given-up course, a clock behind that row's stamp, and an upload while the choice is open on another device, so it is rare and costs an edit in a course the owner is giving up. The second gap in the same 03 sentence: new rows in flight are also invisible. In stress S1 keep_course returned kept 20 of 20 times while a batch of new rows for that course was uncommitted. 03 says 'What the check cannot see is an edit of an existing row still being written in the instant it runs'. Disposition is yours: either make a same-stamp edit visible, or correct the sentence to name both cases.
qolFindings.reproduction: pgr3.mjs in my scratchpad's b7di/r2/, case E and the concurrency cases; pgr3d.mjs in the same folder, case S1. Real migrations on embedded Postgres, UTF-8 database.

qolFindings.title: keep_course can still deadlock against a batch upload of child rows; no data is harmed
qolFindings.evidence: DI-B7-R2-2's course-row shape is fixed (see anglesTried). The remaining cycle is outside it: a batch upsert locks an existing child row, then its end-of-statement foreign key check on a new row waits for the course row keep_course holds FOR UPDATE, while the cascade waits for that child row. Child tables take no advisory lock. S1 used 1 existing row plus 120 new ones, with jitter. Final tally on an idle machine: {kept | write 40P01: 20 of 20}. An earlier run under load sampled every fifth round and also showed the keep losing: 'err 40P01 | write ok | K+X'. In both outcomes the loser rolls back cleanly, and exactly the expected courses remain. By reading src/backup/session.ts, not by running PostgREST: a keep that loses should arrive as status 500 if PostgREST maps 40P01 that way, which keepCourse reads as 'no-answer'. That text says the choice may or may not have arrived, and asking again works. The upload that loses is retried and should then meet the tombstone or a missing course; I did not run that retry.
qolFindings.reproduction: pgr3d.mjs in my scratchpad's b7di/r2/, case S1: a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT of an existing row plus new rows, racing keep_course from a second connection.

qolFindings.title: The two sides sort differently for an astral character against U+E000 to U+FFFF, which gives a permanent CVNEW on that course
qolFindings.evidence: src/persistence/courseFingerprint.ts sorts by UTF-16 code units; keep_course sorts with collate "C", which is UTF-8 byte order. Case D5, with ids 'a' + U+1F600 and 'a' + U+FFFD and matching rows on both sides: 'error CVNEW', and it would repeat on every attempt. D6 (astral id alone), D7 (NFC and NFD) and D2 (accents, quotes, backslash) all kept. Reach is low: app ids are randomUUID values or JSON keys built from ids, and the duty item values I traced are ids chosen by switches, so only a crafted or foreign imported id gets here. Keeping that course instead of giving it up still works. Neither pin covers it: the pinned test value has no such pair. Sorting by code point, or by encoded bytes, closes it.
qolFindings.reproduction: pgr3.mjs in my scratchpad's b7di/r2/, case D5, using the app's own courseFingerprint against the real function.

results.resetOnTheChoice: Observed with an unsent change, offline: afterwards localStorage is empty, the database is gone from indexedDB, the fake server still has 2 courses and the student row unchanged, and the reset itself sent no keep and no course delete (the log's single DELETE, on erased_courses, also appears in the run with no reset). Riapri online: backupState signed-out, 'Crea il corso', 0 courses, meta holds only data:minimumWriter and data:version. The unsent change is lost, as the warning says.
results.sessionSurvival: The normal path does not bring it back. r3c, on a session close to expiry with a short-lived token answer: the key stayed absent for 132 s after the reset, with 0 refresh calls in that run; a first run (with 1 refresh before the reset) stayed absent for 173 s. Riapri then reached signed-out 'Crea il corso'. A refresh already in flight at the moment of the reset was not exercised.
results.killDuringReset: Simulated a kill after the database delete and before the storage clear: the session and sync hint survive with an empty database. On reopen meta is rebuilt with local:awaiting-account-course and local:sync-mode, and the screen is 'Apertura del corso…'. Not corrupt, just a reset that did not finish signing out, and by design the download should refill it and return to the choice. That last step is inferred: the fake refuses sync.
